newsitem.title: USA: Convicted 'Zucchini Bandit' gets long sentence.
newsitem.headline: Convicted 'Zucchini Bandit' gets long sentence.

text.p: After four trials spanning two years, the so-called "Zucchini Bandit" who was convicted of using that vegetable in a robbery has been sentenced to a minimum of 18 years in jail.

Carlos Diaz, also known as Fulton Guevara, was first arrested in April 1995 after restaurant worker Oscar Leal identified him as the man who ordered him to hand over his wristwatch and $20 or he would shoot.
Police officials said they found the stolen goods on Diaz's person -- along with a zucchini he had hidden in his leather jacket, pretending it was a gun.
State Supreme Court Judge Randall Eng handed down the sentence in a Queens courtroom Tuesday, giving Diaz 18 years to life in prison. A jury convicted Diaz in March of second-degree robbery.
Defence attorney Steven Silberblatt called the sentence "outrageous," adding that the normal maximum sentence for second-degree robbery is 7 1/2 to 15 years.

"The violence in this case was minimal," Silberblatt said on Wednesday in a telephone interview. "(Diaz) is a crackhead. He's not a particularly violent guy." Silberblatt said he will appeal the sentence.

Diaz was sentenced under a New York State statute that condemns "persistent" felony offenders to a minimum of 15 years in jail. Diaz has previously been convicted of six felonies, including assault and peddling drugs.

The first "Zucchini Bandit" hearing ended in a mistrial during deliberations; two consecutive trials ended with hung juries. Prosecutors announced in October that they would take the unusual step of trying Diaz a fourth time.
Diaz consistently pleaded innocent and claimed he was simply out shopping for vegetables.
